quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots before changing lanes by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When another car has bright headlights coming toward you, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the bright lights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to light up the road and objects.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive slowly and reduce your speed. Do not use high beam headlights. Low beams light up the road and objects better in fog.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: A driver can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if there is a passing lane available. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and surrounding vehicles. This gives you time to react to mistakes made by other drivers.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can get out of your way.
Must honk your horn so other vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or crossing pedestrians. Failure to stop is unlawful.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Continue to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, continue to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: How fast people usually drive in the area
The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive
How fast to drive in heavy traffic
How fast to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest or slowest speed allowed on the road. The speed limit is for normal conditions. You must slow down when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming car. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming car at least half of the road.
Tell the other car to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming car at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give the oncoming car at least half of the road space. Both cars need enough room to pass safely.

questions.question: On a long drive, what helps reduce tiredness?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours to take a short break on long drives. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and take a nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other cars from your direction.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You may use your horn when:

options.text: You have to stop quickly.
You are passing another car.
Your car is out of control.
You are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your car is out of control.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when your car is out of control. This warns other drivers of danger.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, it is usually best to:

options.text: Go slowly while waiting for an opening.
Speed up faster than traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This helps you merge safely and smoothly. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: You must change your speed for:

options.text: The condition of the road.
The weather.
Other traffic.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving conditions are not ideal. This includes bad road conditions, bad weather, time of day, narrow roads, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: When you must stop at an intersection but see no stop line or crosswalk, you should:

options.text: Not stop at all.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the other road.
Stop where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the other road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the other road.
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point to the other road where you can see traffic. Do not enter the other road to get a better view.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car may take longer to stop than it would on dry roads.
